task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hello, yes... I'm having trouble with my phone. My mobile data isn't working properly — sometimes it stops working completely, and other times it's just very slow. I'd really like to get it fixed, please.

turns.thought: I'd be happy to help you get your mobile data working again. To pull up your account and check the line, could you please provide the phone number of the line that's having trouble?
turns.execution_output:
User: Yes, of course. My phone number is 555-123-2002. The name on the account is John Smith.

I should also mention — I'm currently abroad, in France. I don't know if that matters, but I thought I should tell you.

turns.thought: I found your line — 555-123-2002, which is active on the Premium Plan. That's very relevant: since you're in France, your line needs international roaming enabled on our side for data to work. Let me check your current cycle usage and roaming status.

I've looked up your account, John. I found your line (555-123-2002) on the Premium Plan (15 GB limit) — you've used 8.7 GB this cycle, so your data limit isn't the problem.

Since you're in France (outside your home network), the most likely cause is roaming. **I've enabled international roaming on your line at no cost** — I've verified it's now active on your account.

Now I need to check a few settings on the phone itself, since roaming also has to be switched on in your device's settings. Could you please check the following on your phone and tell me what you see:

1. **Airplane Mode** — is it ON? If so, please turn it OFF.
2. **Mobile data** — in Settings, is mobile data turned ON?
3. **Data Roaming** — in Settings (usually under Mobile Network / Cellular), is "Data Roaming" turned ON? Please turn it ON if it's off.
4. **Signal indicator** — what do you see in the status bar at the top (e.g., "No Signal", 1–4 bars, and the network type like 5G/4G/3G/E)?
5. **Data Saver** — is Data Saver mode ON?
6. **VPN** — are you connected to a VPN?

Let me know what you find and I'll take it from there.
turns.execution_output:
User: Oh my, that's a lot of things to check. Let me try... I'll look at my phone now.

Let me check a few of those things.

turns.thought:
Good information — that's very helpful, and I can see two clear issues. Let's take it one step at a time.

**Step 1: Turn Data Roaming ON**

This is the first and most important fix. I've already enabled roaming on your line from my side, but your phone also has its own Data Roaming switch, and right now it's off — which is why your data stops working entirely while you're in France.

On your phone, please go to:
- **Settings → Mobile Network (or Cellular) → Data Roaming** and turn it **ON**.

**Then restart your phone** (power it off and back on) so the change takes full effect.

Once it's back on, please check the top of your screen again and tell me:
- Do you now see signal bars and a network type (like 4G or 5G) instead of "Poor"/"2G"?
- Does mobile data now work when you open a browser?

**Don't worry about the other items yet** — we'll deal with the "2G" network setting (which is what's making things slow when it *does* work) right after this, since 2G is far too slow for normal browsing. And we'll look at the VPN after that if things are still slow.

Go ahead with Step 1 and let me know what you see.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll try. Let me turn on that Data Roaming thing first.

turns.thought: Let me check one more thing on your account before I guide you further.

turns.thought:
You didn't do anything wrong at all — turning on Data Roaming was still the right move, and it stays on for the rest of your trip. What you're seeing now is a *separate* problem that's hiding behind it: your phone is locked onto **2G**, which is an old, very slow network type. That alone explains both the slowness and the constant dropouts, and it will keep happening regardless of roaming until we change it.

**Step 2: Change your phone's preferred network mode**

Please do this on your phone:
- Go to **Settings → Mobile Network (or Cellular / Connections) → Network Mode** (it may be called "Preferred network type" or "Network mode").
- It's currently set to something like "2G only." Please change it to the option that includes 4G/5G — usually labelled **"5G/4G/3G auto"** or **"4G preferred."**
- Then **restart your phone** again so it reconnects to the network with the new setting.

After it restarts, check the top of the screen once more — you should hopefully see more bars and "4G" or "5G" instead of "2G."

**Step 3 (only if it's still slow): turn the VPN off**

I also noted your VPN is ON and connected. A VPN can slow data down significantly, especially while roaming. Once you've done Step 2, if data is still sluggish, please turn the VPN off temporarily (in Settings → VPN, or by opening your VPN app and disconnecting) and see whether things speed up.

**How to tell if it's working:** after the restart, open your web browser and try loading any website (for example a news site). If a page loads, mobile data is working. If you'd like, you can also run a speed test in the browser and tell me roughly what speed it shows.

Go ahead with Step 2 and let me know what the status bar shows afterwards. We'll go one step at a time.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, let me try to change that network mode thing. I'll see if I can find it.

turns.thought:
That's great news — four bars, "Excellent," and "5G" is exactly what we wanted to see. The network mode change was the fix for the slowness and dropouts.

To answer your questions:

1. **Yes, please restart the phone one more time** — just as you did before. It's a normal step that lets the phone fully lock onto the 5G connection, and it won't undo anything we've set up.

2. **Leave the VPN ON for now.** Don't worry about it. A VPN only needs to be switched off if things are *still* slow after everything else is fixed — and your connection is showing "Excellent," so there's no reason to touch it. You haven't messed anything up.

After the restart, please try opening your web browser and loading a website — that's the real test. Let me know:
- Does the page load?
- Does the status bar still show "Excellent" / 5G?

If browsing works, you're all set. If it's still slow or not loading, tell me and we'll look at the VPN next.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'll restart it again.

turns.thought:
Very glad to hear it — four bars, "Excellent," and "5G" after the restart is a strong sign the connection is stable and healthy.

**How to check the speed properly:**

Since you're on the phone itself, the simplest way is:
1. Open your web browser and go to a speed test site (such as **fast.com** or **speedtest.net**).
2. Tap the start/"GO" button and wait about 20–30 seconds.
3. It will show a **download speed in Mbps**.

As a rough guide for what you'll see:
- **Under 1 Mbps** — very slow; basic web pages will struggle.
- **1–5 Mbps** — will load web pages, but video will be poor and may keep pausing.
- **5–25 Mbps** — good; comfortable browsing and standard-definition video.
- **25 Mbps and above** — excellent; streaming in high definition and video calls with no trouble.

Try that and tell me the number it shows. If it comes back in the "good" or "excellent" range, we're done — and I'd say you can consider this fixed.

One thing to keep in mind: since you're roaming in France, your speed is partly determined by the local French partner network you're connected to, so it may vary a little from place to place. That's normal.

**Summary of what we did today:**
- Enabled international roaming on your line (at no cost) — needed while you're abroad.
- Turned on **Data Roaming** in your phone's settings.
- Changed your **Network Mode** from 2G to 4G/5G — this was the main cause of the slowness and dropouts.
- Left your **VPN on**, since it wasn't causing a problem.

Your line is active, your data usage is 8.7 GB of your 15 GB plan, and you have no overdue bills affecting service.

Go ahead and run the speed test when you get a moment, and let me know the result.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me try that speed test thing.

turns.thought:
That's a genuinely good result — and it's worth clarifying one thing before we go further.

**About "Good" vs "Excellent":** the 25 Mbps+ figure I gave you was my rough guide; "Good" is that particular speed test app's own label, and the two scales don't match up exactly. A result of 27.50 Mbps is solidly in the range that supports HD streaming and video calls. Your phone's signal itself is reporting **"Excellent"** — that's the strongest indicator available.

**On the VPN — yes, it's worth testing.** You remembered correctly. A VPN routes your traffic through an extra server, and that can reduce speed, particularly while roaming on a foreign network. It's a reasonable next thing to try.

Good news on your concern: **turning the VPN off will not touch your photos or anything else stored on your phone.** It's purely a network connection setting — it doesn't delete or move any files.

To test it:
1. Open your VPN app (or go to **Settings → VPN**) and **disconnect**.
2. Run the same speed test again.
3. Compare the two numbers.

Then:
- **If the speed goes up** — you've found the remaining slowdown. You can leave the VPN off while you're in France, or switch it back on any time; nothing is lost either way.
- **If it's about the same** — then the VPN isn't the cause, and this is simply what the local French partner network is delivering at your location. I have no further changes available on my side, and I'd rather tell you that honestly than have you keep chasing it.

Either way, the original fault **is** fixed: your line was set to 2G, which was the reason your data kept stopping and crawling. That setting is now changed permanently, so that specific problem shouldn't come back. If you ever see "2G" in your status bar again, check that same Network Mode setting.

Try the VPN test and let me know the number you get.
turns.execution_output: User: Okay, I'll try turning that VPN thing off. You're sure it won't touch my photos? Alright... here goes.

turns.thought:
That's wonderful — 275 Mbps and "Excellent" is a dramatic improvement, and you've confirmed the VPN was the second cause of the slowdown. So there were two separate problems all along: the phone being stuck on **2G** (which made data stop and crawl) and the **VPN** (which capped your speed). Both are now resolved, and you fixed them yourself on the device.

**To answer your questions:**

**1. Should you leave the VPN off?**
That's your call, and here's the trade-off so you can decide:
- **With the VPN off:** you get the full speed of the local network — which is what you're seeing now.
- **With the VPN on:** your internet traffic is encrypted, but as you've just experienced, it can reduce your speed significantly.

You can switch it back on at any time — it's a single toggle, and turning it off did not change any settings on your account or phone. Nothing has been cancelled or permanently disabled.

**2. Will your data and photos be okay?**
Yes, absolutely. Disconnecting a VPN only stops routing your internet traffic through it. It does not delete, move, or change anything stored on your phone — your photos, messages, and apps are completely untouched. You haven't broken anything; nothing you did today was destructive.

**3. One thing worth keeping in mind:**
With faster speeds, your phone can use data more quickly than before. Your line is at 8.7 GB of your 15 GB plan allowance, and your current billing cycle ends **28 February 2025**. If you use all 15 GB, data will slow or stop until the next cycle — you can check this any time by asking me.

**Summary of your visit:**
| What we found | What we did |
|---|---|
| No international roaming on your line | Enabled roaming (free) |
| Data Roaming off in phone settings | You turned it ON |
| Phone locked to 2G network | You changed Network Mode to 4G/5G |
| VPN reducing speed | You disconnected it |

Please do restart your phone one final time to make sure everything settles in, and enjoy your trip to France! If anything changes — or if you see "2G" or "Poor" in the status bar again — just let me know and I'll look at your line right away.
